title: build-plan.imported — the honestly-empty Build payload an imported native plan carries
description: What a plan carries in place of a Build payload when it arrived as an accepted native Claude or Codex plan and nobody has decomposed it yet. It is deliberately the SMALLEST document the Build plan reader will accept: a version and an empty work-item list, and nothing else. The point is the `maxItems: 0` — this schema does not merely permit an empty decomposition, it FORBIDS a non-empty one, so an import can never quietly write work items nobody authored. A native plan's prose is not a graph, and deriving one from it at import time would produce exactly the fabricated decomposition the Plan Coordinator exists to prevent: plausible node names with no mandate behind them, carrying a reviewer's trust they never earned. The gaps go into the revision's `deliberation.unresolved_decisions` instead, where the seal already refuses while any remain. A payload of this version can be held, shown, revised and diffed; it can never be sealed (plan_contract.SEALABLE_BUILD_PLAN_VERSION is build-plan.v2) and so it can never reach a Build. The way forward is `plan revise` with a real build-plan.v2 payload — authored, not inferred.

work_items.description: Empty, and only ever empty. Present at all — rather than omitted — because the Build plan reader's work-item-id uniqueness layer reads this key on every version, and a payload shape that made that layer raise KeyError would be a reader bug disguised as a schema decision.
